record.original_question: For partially analytic functions, meaning functions whose level lines are real analytic even though the function may have only finite Sobolev regularity across levels, what natural mathematical structure should replace the vector-space structure that fails under addition?

artifact.status_search_result: No literature was found proposing a definitive replacement for the vector-space structure on partially analytic functions (functions with real analytic level sets but only finite Sobolev regularity transverse to levels). The question is posed as an "important problem to find" such a structure, and a targeted web search returned no resolution.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems (zbMATH listing)
status_evidence.snippet: Open-problem survey discussing partially analytic functions and the search for a natural structure replacing addition.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as open in the survey of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics.

status_evidence.title: Web search results on partially analytic functions
status_evidence.snippet: No results addressing a substitute algebraic structure for partially analytic functions were found.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution or follow-up work proposing such a structure was located.
